subject: Re: Order Form — invoice entity, aggregation and tax reclamation process
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acme-corp.com>, Finance AP <finance@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form — confirming invoice entity, PO mapping & tax expectations

Hi Sarah / Finance team,

Quick follow on the order form redlines we sent yesterday (attached as Draft_OrderForm_Redlines.docx). To finalize the invoice path we need confirmation on three items so legal/finance can close the commercial:

1) Invoice entity: which legal entity should Redwood invoice? (we have two on file: Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) and Redwood Inference EMEA Ltd.) Please indicate exact legal name and billing address that should appear on the invoice.

2) PO / aggregation: your PO (Acme PO #8912) indicates a single PO for multiple purchases. Do you want monthly consolidated invoices against that PO or per-delivery invoices tagged to the same PO? Consolidated invoices will change tax/residency treatment in some jurisdictions.

3) Withholding / VAT: does Acme intend to apply any withholding tax on payments to Redwood? If yes, please confirm the expected percentage and whether you will provide withholding certificates to allow tax credit/recovery on your side. If VAT applies, confirm the registration number and whether you require VAT-exclusive or VAT-inclusive invoicing.

If you prefer, we can do a 20–30 minute call to nail these details — they affect payment terms, net-terms setup, and whether we need an entity fallback clause in the order form (suggested language below).

Suggested fallback wording (for your team to review):
"If the invoicing entity specified by Customer is unable to accept invoices due to tax residency or entity transfer restrictions, Customer shall notify Redwood and provide an alternate entity within 10 business days. Until Customer provides an alternate invoice entity, Redwood may suspend issuance of new invoices for the affected amounts and work in good faith to route invoicing through an agreed entity."

Thanks — want to avoid surprises during invoice cutover.

Best,
Ben
Senior Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_OrderForm_Redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Finance AP <finance@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form — confirming invoice entity, PO mapping & tax expectations

Thanks Ben — looping in AP (finance@acme-corp.com) and procurement for specifics. Quick answers below, pending AP confirmation:

1) Invoice entity: Invoice should be issued to Acme Cloud Services, LLC (Acme CLS). Billing address is in the PO (see attached).

2) PO mapping: We prefer monthly consolidated invoices tied to PO #8912. That keeps our AP process simpler; please include a line on each invoice noting the PO number and the period covered.

3) Withholding / VAT: Acme does not anticipate withholding on payments to Redwood for the US entity. If Redwood invoices from an offshore entity, there's a chance AP will apply withholding — we will confirm. For VAT, Acme is not VAT-registered in the US; VAT should not apply to USD invoices.

One ask: can Redwood include your tax ID and our PO number in the invoice footer? AP requires the mapping for automated reconciliation. Also, can you share wiring instructions PDF?

Sarah
Sr. Manager, Strategic Procurement
Acme Corp

Attachment referenced: Acme_PO_8912.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Order Form — confirming invoice entity, PO mapping & tax expectations

Forwarding Acme's reply. A couple internal notes:

- PO mapping: they want monthly consolidated invoices for PO #8912. That suggests we set up an invoice cadence (monthly arrears) instead of per-delivery billing. We should confirm our minimum commit recognition schedule so revenue ops can match.

- Withholding risk: Sarah flagged the possibility if we invoice from a non-US entity. Kimberly — can legal confirm if we can add contractual language that requires the customer to use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid withholding and to provide certificates where applicable? We can attach an exhibit for tax evidence.

- Invoice footer: AP asks for our tax ID + PO number on each invoice. Finance prefers the invoice footer template in Wiring_Instructions_v2.pdf; attaching for reference.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to propose narrow redline for the Order Form: "customer cooperation for tax evidence / withholding certificates" + entity fallback timeline (10 business days).
2) Ben to confirm invoice cadence and whether consolidated monthly billing aligns with minimum commit recognition and invoicing triggers.
3) I will draft final invoice template and circulate.

Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Wiring_Instructions_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acme-corp.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Apr 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form — confirming invoice entity, PO mapping & tax expectations

Sarah / Acme team — thanks for the quick responses and the PO. A few legal clarifications and proposed redline language below (short and narrow, intended to avoid procurement delays):

1) Invoice entity: confirming Redwood will invoice Acme Cloud Services, LLC (as provided). Please confirm the exact legal name as it appears on the PO and the W-9/IRS docs if available.

2) Withholding / tax certificates: if Acme withholds any tax, Redwood requests customer to provide official withholding certificates within 30 days of payment date so Redwood may claim a foreign tax credit or refund. Suggested clause:

"If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold or deduct taxes from payments due to Redwood, Customer shall (a) notify Redwood promptly, (b) provide Redwood with official documentation of the tax withheld (e.g., withholding certificate) within thirty (30) days of payment, and (c) where commercially feasible, cooperate in good faith to minimize such withholdings."

3) Entity fallback: minimal change to order form to permit short suspension of new invoice issuance (not service). We will not use this to delay collections; language is limited to routing/administrative delays.

4) Invoice aggregation and recognition: commercial ops (Ben / Marissa) — please confirm whether monthly consolidated invoices align with your recognition and whether minimum commit billing should still be triggered per month or on a per-delivery basis. If minimum commit is based on monthly usage, consolidated invoices are fine. If not, we need a split-invoice approach to preserve month-by-month recognition.

If you approve the redlines, I will incorporate them in Draft_OrderForm_Redlines.docx and send back for signature. Otherwise, suggest a 15m sync early next week.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Cc: Legal Ops; Revenue Ops
